content: 1. Valerian, when used in combination with alfentanil, increases sedation. It is recommended to avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 2. Valerian and alprazolam both enhance sedative effects. Avoid co-administration or consider alternative therapies. 3. Valerian increases the effects of amobarbital through pharmacodynamic synergy, leading to heightened sedation. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 4. Valerian and atracurium both increase sedation. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 5. Valerian increases the effects of belinostat by reducing its metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. Strong UGT inhibitors decrease belinostat metabolism; reduce the starting dose of belinostat to 750 mg/m² when co-administered with UGT inhibitors or in patients homozygous for the UGT1A128 allele. 6. Valerian and buprenorphine (including buccal, subdermal implant, and transdermal forms) increase sedation. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 7. Valerian increases the effects of butabarbital and butalbital through pharmacodynamic synergy, leading to increased sedation. Avoid these combinations or use alternative drugs. 8. Valerian and chloral hydrate both enhance sedation. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 9. Valerian increases the effects of citalopram, leading to increased sedation. Use caution and monitor the patient closely. 10. Valerian increases the effects of dexmedetomidine through pharmacodynamic synergy, which may enhance CNS depression. Use caution and monitor the patient. 11. Valerian increases the effects of diphenhydramine and hydroxyzine through pharmacodynamic synergy, potentially enhancing CNS depression. Use caution and monitor the patient. 12. Valerian and fentanyl (including intranasal, transdermal, and transmucosal forms) both increase sedation. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 13. Valerian and gabapentin both enhance sedative effects. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 14. Valerian increases the effects of imipramine and nortriptyline, leading to increased sedation. Use caution and monitor the patient. 15. Valerian increases the effects of phenobarbital through pharmacodynamic synergy, which may enhance CNS depression. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 16. Valerian and tramadol both increase sedation. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 17. Valerian increases the effects of zolpidem and zaleplon, leading to increased sedation. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 18. Valerian increases the effects of irinotecan by decreasing its metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown, but caution is advised. 19. Valerian increases the effects of azelastine through pharmacodynamic synergy, which may enhance CNS depression. Use caution and monitor the patient. 20. Valerian and midazolam (including intranasal forms) both increase sedation and may lead to profound or prolonged drug effects, including hypoventilation or airway obstruction. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 21. Valerian and lasmiditan both increase sedation. Co-administration may lead to additive impairment of psychomotor performance. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 22. Valerian and lemborexant both increase sedation. Dosage adjustment may be necessary due to potentially additive effects. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 23. Valerian increases the effects of tricyclic antidepressants (e.g., amitriptyline, clomipramine, trimipramine) and SSRIs (e.g., fluoxetine, sertraline, escitalopram), leading to increased sedation. Use caution and monitor the patient. 24. Valerian increases the effects of CNS depressants, including narcotics, hypnotics, and sedatives, which may result in additive neuropsychiatric side effects. Avoid use and monitor patients for excessive CNS toxicity. 25. Valerian increases the effects of promethazine and chlorpheniramine through pharmacodynamic synergy, potentially enhancing CNS depression. Use caution and monitor the patient. These statements provide detailed, professional guidance on the interactions and precautions associated with valerian use.
